drawings.description: en marge gauche, sous la note oblique, un petit schéma de relations : $F' \ll F$ au-dessus de $G' \ll G$, un signe d'inclusion vertical ($\cup$) sous $F'$ et un autre sous $F$.
drawings.notes: F' << F above G' << G, a vertical inclusion sign (cup) under F' and another under F, as on the page. The F' is written over another letter (it looks overwritten); read F' as in the transcription. Left out: the fragments of the oblique marginal note above and to the left (text, not part of the schema). Nothing struck. Method: a relation diagram of formulas, which the transcription skill would set as text (tikz-cd); since it stands only as a \drawing mark, it is set here as a TikZ layout of the formula: every symbol is a LaTeX text node at its place on the page, the arrows are drawn between them. drawings.description: moitié gauche, premier schéma, entièrement biffé (surchargé et barré de traits obliques) : \ill{} $\to F' \subset \overline{F}' \xrightarrow{\sim} F$ au-dessus de $\overline{G}' \xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{G}' \subset \overline{G} \simeq G$, avec des inclusions verticales.

What can be seen under the strokes: a scribbled symbol, -> F' (included in) F-bar' ~-> F on the top row, G-bar' ~-> G-bar' (included in) G-bar ~ G on the bottom row, with vertical inclusions, as the transcription says. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: moitié gauche, deuxième schéma : $\Phi \subset \overline{F}'' \xrightarrow{\sim} F' \subset \overline{F}' \xrightarrow{\sim} F$ au-dessus de $\overline{G}'' \xrightarrow{\sim} G' \subset \overline{G} \xrightarrow{\sim} G$, avec des flèches verticales descendantes.
drawings.notes: Top row: Phi (included in) F-bar'' ~-> F' (included in) F-bar' ~-> F; bottom row, a little lower on the left: G-bar'' ~-> G' (included in) G-bar ~-> G; a descending vertical arrow under each of the four nodes F-bar'', F', F-bar', F. Labels after the transcription. Doubtful: on the crop the first top node shows one prime only (F-bar', the transcription has F-bar''), the third top node shows a bar with a small arrow over it and no clear prime (the transcription has F-bar'), and the first bottom node shows one prime (transcription G-bar''). Left out as struck: the scribbled insertion above F' (an F-bar with a ~ and an arrow, struck through). Method: a relation diagram of formulas, which the transcription skill would set as text (tikz-cd); since it stands only as a \drawing mark, it is set here as a TikZ layout of the formula: every symbol is a LaTeX text node at its place on the page, the arrows are drawn between them. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Revised 2026-11-11 after Michel's check (#142): the primes of the first top and bottom nodes are one each, F-bar prime and G-bar prime, as on the crop; the third top node is still to check. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): the third top node has no prime on the page: an F under a bar with a small arrow added over it. The cube at the foot of the same page has the same chain F' included in F-vec ~-> F, with F-vec standing over G-bar, so the node is F-vec, and it is now set so (the bar is the first writing, the arrow the correction). Not checked by a reader.
drawings.disagreement: Michel, #142: the primes of the first top and bottom nodes are one each, F-bar prime and G-bar prime, as on the crop. The third top node has no prime: it is an F-bar with an arrow added, i.e. F-vec as in the cube below; the transcription has F-bar prime.

drawings.description: moitié gauche, troisième schéma : $\overline{F}' \subset \widetilde{F} \xrightarrow{\sim} \vec{F} \xrightarrow{\sim} F$ au-dessus de $\widetilde{G} \xrightarrow{\sim} \overline{G} \xrightarrow{\sim} G$, avec des flèches verticales.

Labels after the transcription; doubtful: the middle bottom node (read G-bar; on the crop it may carry a tilde as well as a bar). Left out: the top of the large arc that encloses the fourth schema, which passes under this one. Nothing struck. Method: a relation diagram of formulas, which the transcription skill would set as text (tikz-cd); since it stands only as a \drawing mark, it is set here as a TikZ layout of the formula: every symbol is a LaTeX text node at its place on the page, the arrows are drawn between them. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: moitié gauche, en bas, entouré d'un grand arc, un cube de relations : en haut $\Phi \subset \overline{F}'$, $\widetilde{F}$, $\vec{F}$, $F$ ; au milieu $F'$ ; en bas $\overline{G}'$, $\widetilde{G}$, $\overline{G}$, $G$, $G'$ ; des flèches marquées $\simeq$ (subdivisions) et des flèches verticales.
drawings.notes: Large arrow diagram, drawn as the skill prescribes for these: nodes placed as on the page, the principal arrows between them, labels as the transcription reads them. Top face: Phi (included in) -> F-bar'; F-bar' to F-tilde by a curved inclusion arrow; F-tilde ~-> F-vec ~-> F. Middle: F', reached from F-bar' by a ~-> arrow and joined to F-vec by a curved inclusion arrow; a vertical stroke from F-tilde down to F'. Bottom face: G-bar', G-tilde ~-> G-bar ~-> G, and G' reached from G-bar' by a ~-> arrow, with a short inclusion hook from G' towards G-bar and from G-bar' towards G-tilde. Vertical strokes: F-bar' down to G-bar', F' down to G-tilde, F-vec down to G-bar, F down to G, and a long vertical from F' down past G-tilde to G'. The large arc that encloses it is drawn. Left out: the heavy hatched scribble at the top (struck), and the F' at the far left joined to it by a double stroke (read as part of that struck insertion; doubtful). Arrowheads and hooks are approximate. Method: a relation diagram of formulas, which the transcription skill would set as text (tikz-cd); since it stands only as a \drawing mark, it is set here as a TikZ layout of the formula: every symbol is a LaTeX text node at its place on the page, the arrows are drawn between them. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): the F' at the far left is crossed by the same double stroke that leads into the hatched scribble, and no arrow of the cube reaches it; the cube needs one F' only, the middle one, which carries the arrows from F-bar' and to F-vec. The far-left F' is struck with the insertion and stays left out. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: en marge droite, un petit schéma : $F$ et $F'$ sur une ligne, reliés par un signe de subdivision surchargé et barré ; sous $F$, un signe d'inclusion vertical ($\cup$), puis $G$ ; sous $F'$, un trait vertical en pointillés, puis $G'$ ; entre $G$ et $G'$, des points.
drawings.notes: F and F' on a line; under F a vertical inclusion sign (cup), then G; under F' a dotted vertical stroke ending in a small blot, then G'; two dots between G and G'. Left out as struck: the subdivision sign between F and F', overwritten and struck, and the long oblique stroke that crosses it (one of the strokes striking the paragraph). The transcription's description matches. Method: a relation diagram of formulas, which the transcription skill would set as text (tikz-cd); since it stands only as a \drawing mark, it is set here as a TikZ layout of the formula: every symbol is a LaTeX text node at its place on the page, the arrows are drawn between them. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): at 700 dpi the sign between F and F' is made of heavy curved strokes written over one another, a curly « precedes or equals » with its point towards F, and is not scribbled out; the only stroke across it is one of the two long thin oblique lines that strike the whole paragraph, which are left out everywhere. The sign is now drawn, and the dots between G and G' are three, as on the page. Not checked by a reader.
drawings.disagreement: The sign between F and F' is overwritten, not struck: the only stroke across it is one of the long obliques that strike the paragraph (the transcription has « surchargé et barré »).
